text:
Stocks start 2018 with gains on strength in technology Associated Press 1 hr ago MARLEY JAY Click to expand Replay Video UP NEXT Caterpillar's $2B tax fight with the IRS could change how US companies do business Federal officials have been investigating Caterpillar Inc.'s taxes and profits processed through its Swiss subsidiary, Caterpillar SARL. CNBC McDonald's dollar menu returns McDonald's is bringing back its Dollar Menu with a new twist. On January 4, McDonald's is officially debuting the "$1 $2 $3 menu." Items that will cost only $1 on the new menu include the sausage burrito, McChicken, cheeseburger, and soft drinks of all sizes Small McCafé drinks will cost only $2, along with other $2 items, and $3 items include The Sausage McMuffin with Eggs, new Classic Chicken Sandwich, Triple Cheeseburger, and Happy Meals. Wochit Business California marijuana market to reach nearly $4 billion in 2018 On January 1, the state of California is set to begin sales of recreational marijuana - a market that is expected to reach $3.7 billion in 2018 alone. Research firm BDS Analytics adds in a report that the number will then increase to over $5 billion the year after. BDS goes on to say that California, which is the world's sixth largest economy, will be a huge chunk of the total North America market for cannabis. Stocks started the new year higher thanks in part to gains in technology and health care companies, some of the market's biggest winners from 2017.

▲ 85.95 +0.41 +0.48% Gilead Sciences Inc GILD
▲ 74.10 +2.46 +3.43% Retailers were also up. Energy stocks rose as natural gas prices jumped because of the cold weather that continues to grip much of the U.S.
KEEPING SCORE: The Standard & Poor's 500 index closed 0.83 percent higher, building on its 19 percent climb in 2017. The Dow ended 104 points higher. The Nasdaq jumped 1.5 percent.
CAN THEY DO IT AGAIN: Facebook and graphics chipmaker Nvidia advanced as technology companies climbed further. The technology index of the S&P 500 surged almost 37 percent last year as big names including Facebook, Apple and Microsoft reached all-time highs. The Nasdaq climbed 28 percent.
Drug and medical device companies led the health care sector higher. Hepatitis C and HIV drug maker Gilead Sciences and Abbott Laboratories, which sells medications, infant formula and medical devices, and Baxter International all rose.
Retailers also climbed. Amazon, Target and Kohl's advanced. Early indications suggest shoppers had a busy holiday season and investors will look for confirmation of those reports in the weeks to come.
BONDS: Bond prices slid. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note rose to 2.47 percent from 2.41 percent. The yield on 2-year note rose to 1.91 percent from 1.89 percent.
The increase in bond yields sent high-dividend stocks like utilities, household goods makers and real estate companies lower. Higher bond yields make those stocks less appealing to investors seeking income.
The Federal Reserve expects to keep raising interest rates this year. If so, it will do it under new leadership, as Fed governor Jerome Powell will replace Chair Janet Yellen in February.
FORCE-FUL PERFORMANCE: On the last day of the year, "Star Wars: The Last Jedi" surpassed "Beauty and the Beast" as the top grossing film in North America in 2017. Its gross will reach $1 billion in the next few days even before the movie opens in China. Both "The Last Jedi" and the live-action "Beauty and the Beast" were made by Disney, which rose $3.43, or 3.2 percent, to $110.96.
NEW YEARS' RESOLUTION: Weight Watchers International climbed after it struck a deal with producer and recording artist DJ Khaled, who will represent the brand to millions of follows on Snapchat, Twitter, Instagram and Facebook. Weight Watchers got a big boost a few years ago from a deal with Oprah Winfrey that also included a substantial investment in the company. Its stock added $2.72, or 6.1 percent, to $47.00.
ENERGY : Benchmark U.S. crude rose 58 cents to $60.42 a barrel in New York. Brent crude, used to price international oils, rose 71 cents to $66.87 barrel in London. A rally late in the year sent crude oil to its highest price since June 2015.
Natural gas futures climbed 10 cents, or 3.6 percent, to $2.738 per 1,000 cubic feet. Natural gas is mostly used to heat homes and demand often rises in frigid weather.
CURRENCY : The dollar fell to 112.11 yen from 112.64 yen. The euro rose to $1.2048 from $1.2012. The dollar declined steadily in 2017 and the ICE U.S. dollar index slumped 10 percent, its biggest decline since 2003. The improved global economy was responsible for much of that decline, however, and the weaker dollar makes U.S. exports less expensive in other markets.
OVERSEAS : Germany's DAX fell 0.4 percent and France's CAC 40 shed 0.5 percent. The British FTSE 100 retreated 0.5 percent.
Asian markets mostly did better. A survey by Chinese business magazine Caixin found manufacturing grew in December at the fastest rate in four months. In India, a survey showed manufacturing hit a five-year high in December. The Hang Seng in Hong Kong gained 2 percent to and Seoul's Kospi gained 0.5 percent. Markets in Japan were closed for a holiday.
